analysis:
Only docs/developer/test.md is supplied (head_text, lines 1-866). The visible change is documentation: a new "App Attest provider dispatch" section (lines 5-22) and a "Last updated: 2026-10-11" header. It describes ServeLoopAppAttestTests and the opt-in ServeLoopAppAttestInteropTests, which run against a loopback coordinator with Apple and model work stubbed by local fixtures. Test callbacks produce signatures for the real verifier, and the doc states these tests do not qualify a signed release on Apple hardware or cover initial Apple enrollment. That limit is consistent with the TB-011 assumptions (T-052, T-053, T-054, T-057); the doc claims no production authorization.

I found no change to runtime authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior in the supplied units. I flagged no new attack surface: the tests use loopback and local fixtures, and the doc names no credentials or secrets.

The canonical context header mentions a provider dispatch availability change (docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#provider-connection-control). Its source code is not in these units, so the next pass should check whether the dispatch change preserves the following. (a) Final-dispatch live expiry and revocation checks (T-053). (b) Connection and endpoint binding of grants (A-016). (c) That a suspended model load cannot extend a grant or bypass revocation. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

The T-041 definition was given in full but this doc change does not touch the SSD cache policy; it only restates existing test guidance (lines 69-95, 282-284, 301-440). The doc says tests keep isolated state and do not overwrite live daemon status files. That is consistent with the existing mitigations.
